result:
There is a peculiar kind of peace in doing something slowly.

Making coffee without rushing. Walking without turning the trip into exercise. Reading a page twice because the first time you were listening more to the rain than to the words. These moments can seem inefficient, but perhaps efficiency is not the right measure for a life.

We often treat time as though it were a substance leaking from a cracked container. Save time. Spend time. Waste time. Run out of time. Yet the minutes we call “wasted” are sometimes the ones that remain vivid: an aimless conversation, a wrong turn into an unfamiliar street, an afternoon when nothing was accomplished except noticing the light move across a wall.

A machine is most valuable when it performs reliably and quickly. A person is not a machine. A person hesitates, wanders, changes their mind, grows attached to impractical things, and occasionally needs an entire day to understand a feeling that arrived in a second.

Maybe that is not a design flaw. Maybe it is the design.
